Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

throw verb

also toss, throw the ball, let fly, hurl

classical

jaciō, jacere

verb, third conjugation

Other words

  • conjiciō, conjicere, conjēcī, conjectum — throw, toss

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 44: pilam conjicere; Traupman 393

  • ēmittō, ēmittere, ēmīsī, ēmissum — let fly, discharge (a missile); let go

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 2.23.1: pīla (Lewis & Short); Traupman 339

Examples

  • Pilam mihi jace.

    Throw me the ball.composed

  • pater eam lēniter conjiciēbat, Theodōrus manibus excipiēbat, aut, sī ēlāpsa erat, pede ad patrem pulsābat

    Dad tossed it gently, Theo caught it in his hands or, if it slipped, kicked it back to DadLibellus IV, Diēs Grātulātiōnis

  • Ibi follem, quem puerī quīdam pede pulsābant, ad sē volūtum Theodōrus ambābus manibus ad eōs conjēcit.

    There some boys were kicking a ball; when it rolled to him Theo threw it back to them with both hands.Libellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

  • pilam (follem) conjicere

    throw the ballTraupman 44

See also catch, kick, ball.

SourcesLewis & Short: conicio · Lewis & Short: emitto
